about_the_game:
Tarnex Warfare is a tactical real-time strategy focused on realism and dynamic frontlines.

Command modern combat units, capture ground, and manage your forces in battles that simulate the chaos and pressure of real warfare. Every decision — from positioning your troops to calling in an airstrike — can shift the tide of the fight.

Unlike traditional RTS games, Tarnex Warfare replaces base building and economy with strategic control, logistics, and morale. The front line moves dynamically based on unit positions and combat results, creating a living, breathing battlefield.

Plan your operations, coordinate infantry, armor, drones, and artillery, and hold your territory against overwhelming odds. Experience modern conflict from a commander’s point of view — a few kilometers of ground can decide the outcome of the war.

Core features:
• Dynamic frontline that reacts to your actions
• Realistic combat simulation with suppression, morale, and terrain impact
• Modular battle system — infantry, vehicles, drones, artillery, and air support
• Satellite-style maps with zoom-based detail
• In-game map editor and custom missions (in development)
• Atmospheric day-night cycle and weather

Tarnex Warfare combines the clarity of tactical maps with the intensity of real-time combat — a modern war experience built for strategists.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10 (64-bit)
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-1035G1 / AMD Ryzen 3 1200 (4 core)
  • Memory: 2 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA MX350 (2GB)
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 2 GB available space
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: Windows 10/11 (64-bit)
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-10400 / AMD Ryzen 5 3600 (6 core)
  • Memory: 4 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GTX 1660 / AMD RX 5600 XT (6 GB)
  • Storage: 8 GB available space

short_description: Command your forces across a dynamic frontline. Capture ground, hold your positions, call in artillery and airstrikes, and reshape the battlefield in this real-time strategy of modern warfare.
